I deal with a lot of clients with domestic violence issues. These are really tough because the way the laws are written it is impossible for victims to get emergency help without tearing the family apart and causing other serious problems for the victim. Abusers take advantage of this by actually showing their victims what will happen if they are reported and guilting them into staying quiet -- sometimes with the help of family, friends, clergy, and so forth. In other cases they take advantage of the laws by reporting minor incidents and getting convictions against their victims; e.g., pressing charges when a DV victim throws a deck of cards at him then taking her down to the courthouse to plead guilty and paying her fine so it is on her record. This is especially effective when your victim is a mail order bride who barely speaks English and understands neither the law nor its consequences and is completely dependent on her husband.

So, let's meet Ann (not her real name obviously), a 42 kg, 153 cm Asian girl in her 30's with long black hair and big glasses -- well educated for her home country with a fairly good command of English but would need an interpreter in a courtroom and is far from being an expert in how our justice system works. Her husband (185 cm, 100+ kg) has been abusing her for years. She's been in the hospital twice, walks with a permanent limp, and has sought help both times she was hospitalized from other agencies but did not follow through and ended up reconciling (she is not stupid, there are cultural and other impediments that people write books about why that happens so often -- see above). So no convictions and no local police reports or arrests.

One day Ann walks into my office. I completely lack the literary skill to convey how she looked: crushed spirit, crushed soul, bruises everywhere; downcast and completely helpless and hopeless. She had tried to stand up to her husband and he decided to show her who is boss. How many times does he have to hit her to make her look like that? Zero. All he had to do is make a BS emergency call and the police raced over to do it for him without so much as a "how do you do?" No resistance. Just two police officers, a 42kg Asian woman, and a brick staircase.

I've seen a lot of crap, but this is the first time I've actually had to fight back tears. The police are generally very professional, but incidents like this completely undermine what a lot of good people and good police officers are trying to accomplish. It is hard to convince real victims to seek help. Really hard. They are scared for themselves, their kids, and their futures. Their self esteem has been eroded by a constant stream of name-calling and ridicule. When victims seek help they have to put an immense amount of faith and trust in everyone involved who have to convince them that there is a future that years of conditioning have told them doesn't exist. Even without youtube videos, incidents like this get around. I have to ask people to trust the police but I also have to be candid with them.
